area: External source GET / HEAD / Git metadata
title: Source refresh did not enforce public HTTPS destinations at each redirect and actual DNS route
reproduction: Baseline source trace at 3837d1951; fixed build verified with local resolver, redirect and nonconnecting socket doubles. No live reproduction or private-service probe.
expected: Only public HTTPS locations and actually selected public IP addresses are eligible on initial requests and all redirect hops. Preserve conditional GET, HEAD, ordinary public redirects and picker-granted local content; never silently bypass a configured proxy.
observed: Baseline admission inspected URL text; source GET had only a downgrade check, generic HEAD had no equivalent policy, and GitHostsJsonApiSource created a bare client. No evidence that an internal service was contacted.
fix: One guarded OkHttp builder for body GET, generic HEAD and Git API metadata GET. Checks each redirect, blocks non-public literals and route DNS answers; fails closed on proxy-first routes including DIRECT fallback. Local content remains separate. Public proxy/enterprise limitation documented in deep-signoff/input-safety.md.
test_evidence: Independent /tmp/adaway-input-net.F6mFtP; 58/58 focused JVM/config tests passed (0 skipped). SourceHttpPolicyTest 9/9; SourceHttpWiringTest 1/1; 48 conditional/directory/Git/backup/SAF regressions. Real OkHttp route planner: denied redirect answer created zero sockets; allowed v4/v6 went only to the recording socket at the exact address. HTTP proxy-first plus DIRECT fallback and required SOCKS both fail closed. Raw log, JUnit XML and tested-input hashes: app/build/reports/audit-2026-11-25/deep-input-net/. No live endpoint, emulator or signed-release claim.

title: Remote metadata had no application-level body limit
reproduction: Source inspection: both metadata clients read the whole HTTP body as a string; the 512 MiB rule-data limit did not apply. Verification uses in-memory streams and terminal HTTP doubles only.
expected: Reject oversized or incomplete metadata before JSON parsing or cache publication, including unknown-length bodies. Preserve last-good directory entries and known Git observations.
observed: Both metadata readers lacked a byte budget. A failed manual Git date observation also flowed to an unconditional DAO write of null. No crash or live-service impact claimed.
fix: 8 MiB decoded bytes for the full directory catalog; 1 MiB each for directory detail/taxonomies and Git API responses. Known oversize rejected without reading; unknown lengths bounded independently. Git failure does not overwrite last-good metadata or dismiss a known pending update. Existing Discover cache writes already follow a complete successful refresh.
